title: Alacritty not updating prompt after a command
body:
I'm pretty new in linux in general and i wanted to install Alacritty since it is much cleaner than the base GNOME terminal, everything works great but im having the next issue;

In some cases, when executing a command (like neofetch or apt install) the terminal takes more time than needed to show the prompt again, similar to using a terminal in a VM. I can make it reaper just by tipping but it is pretty annoying, since in the GNOME terminal this doesn't happen.

[Grabación de pantalla desde 28-09-23 22:50:38.webm](https://github.com/alacritty/alacritty/assets/38926828/7b2e593e-437b-479f-b576-cb61c7d03292)

### System

OS: Linux Mint 21.2
Version: alacritty 0.13.0-dev (a58fb39b)
Linux/BSD: X11

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: Could you post a log with `-vv`?

comments.body:

Interestingly when I try to record the problem using [peek](https://github.com/phw/peek) the problem does'nt happen.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
You don't have to _install_ unless you want to daily drive it. Follow the https://github.com/alacritty/alacritty/blob/master/INSTALL.md (without actually installing).

To test you'll have a point where you'd need to run `cargo`, at this point, apply the patch with `git apply -3` and run `cargo run --release`, then try to repro your issue. 

I kind of can repro this issue with llvmpipe on gnome(but not on i3 outside of gnome) and my patch fixes it, but after talking to mesa developers we think that it's a gnome bug, since the patch doesn't make any sense at all.

I'll try the suggested patch on my daily machine and let you know soon how I've experienced it after applying the patch. I have it installed now on master:

I just saved the content to a file (test.patch) that I stored in the root folder and then applied it with:
``` bash

```

comments.author: participant6
comments.body:
Also, be careful with your default x-terminal-emulator. If you compile and use a local version, it'll use that if you have it in your PATH prior to the distro path, but if you spawn alacritty with your desktop managers shortcut, it's likely using the one specified by `x-terminal-emulator`. I.e, if you intend to just try a local copy of alacritty, consider also updating the default `x-terminal-emulator`.

```bash
$ sudo update-alternatives --install /usr/bin/x-terminal-emulator x-terminal-emulator /home/<user>/bin/alacritty 60
update-alternatives: using /home/<user>/bin/alacritty to provide /usr/bin/x-terminal-emulator (x-terminal-emulator) in auto mode
```
After that I have
```
$ sudo update-alternatives --config x-terminal-emulator
There are 8 choices for the alternative x-terminal-emulator (providing /usr/bin/x-terminal-emulator).

  Selection    Path                             Priority   Status
------------------------------------------------------------
* 0            /home/<user>/bin/alacritty           60        auto mode
  1            /home/<user>/bin/alacritty           60        manual mode
  2            /usr/bin/alacritty                50        manual mode
...
```

I noticed this when my colorscheme didn't apply. I.e., the `*.toml` files weren't loading, which is what is used for configurations of newer versions of alacritty.
